title: The 120 s media-tree refresh re-reads every pool clip's proxy state through Resolve, unchanged pool or not
what: _enrich_proxy_keys asks Resolve for Proxy Media Path and Proxy (plus Frames for archive clips) on every pool clip every 120 s with no memory of the previous pass; each 100-clip chunk reconnects, and the uid map (60 s TTL < 120 s refresh) is rebuilt in one lock hold. Without a library the API walk does 5 RPCs per clip in a single _API_LOCK hold.
cost: In-tree measurement 5.5 s per 1,298 clips. Today 5-17 s of Resolve API time per 120 s at idle. At 20,000 clips ~85 s reads + ~2.3 s single-hold uid walk + 200 connects per pass (~80 % of Resolve's scripting capacity); API-fallback machines hold _API_LOCK ~145 s per pass (estimated from 9.4 s / 1,298).
evidence: resolve_bridge.py:1929-1935, :2006-2030, :2139 vs app.py:2102; GOTCHAS section 16; proxy_relink.py:835 only acts on non-working proxies.
fix: Memo uid -> (proxy_path, proxy_state, frames) per project; re-read only new clips, clips whose last state was not working, or after ProjectLibrary.changed(); full re-read every Nth pass; uid-map TTL above the refresh interval. Keep the no-half-enriched-list contract and keep enrichment off _LIBRARY_LOCK.

title: Every bridge call opens a brand-new scriptapp() connection (1/s with the Cards role, every 3 s from the watcher, per enrichment chunk, per relinked clip)
what: connect() calls scriptapp('Resolve') every time with no cached handle: a TCP connect to 1144, a HostApp create/destroy in fuscript, a second connection to Resolve, a TIME_WAIT socket. The Cards engine in the same process holds one steady connection, yet its 1 s sweep reconnects through library_timeline_items -> _timeline_head_locked.
cost: 75 ms per guarded connect and 49 TIME_WAIT sockets measured in LAG-INVESTIGATION.md:138-148/:418. Watcher ~1.3 s/min of lock time connecting; Cards role +~4 s/min; a 1,300-op relink +~85 s; a 20k enrichment pass +200 connects.
evidence: resolve_bridge.py:452 and module docstring lines 7-9; LAG-INVESTIGATION.md:54-55, :145-146; MulticamPipeline cards/resolve_engine.py:265.
fix: Cache the scriptapp object keyed on the fuscript listener pid and Resolve pid script_server already sees; reuse while every probe answers READY with the same pids; drop on non-READY, pid change, any exception, or GetProjectManager() None. Keeps CR-68 and R12 (stale-bridge restart still fires).

title: The watcher stats and realpaths every timeline clip every 3 s, even when the Resolve answer came from the poll cache
what: Every poll reclassifies every item; for canonical-prefix clips not textually under local_root (every clip on a remote editor rig, where P: is the \\localhost\CCSync_P loopback share) that is one exists() and, for present files, one realpath() through the SMB redirector per clip per poll. The per-file realpath is redundant when the cached prefix check passes.
cost: Measured 2,000 files on local NTFS: 57 ms exists + 102 ms realpath = ~160 ms per 3 s poll (~5 % of a core continuously); through loopback SMB estimated 3-10x (0.5-1.6 s per poll). At 20k items it no longer fits the 3 s interval.
evidence: probe classify_probe.py; paths.py:158-163 (_delooped); watcher.py:169-171 memoises the archive/proxy questions but not the classification.
ledger: related to comp-resolve-7 (2026-09-18, FIXED, different question)
fix: Test the cached prefix verdict before the per-file realpath, and memoise path -> OK/MISSING across polls with the _exempt_memo TTL/cap, dropped on the bridge's full walk. Keep BAD_PREFIX detection; never memoise OUT_OF_TREE/FOREIGN offers.

title: A project switch runs one full media-pool walk per pending file move, synchronously on the watcher thread
what: _relink_pending_moves calls relink_moved once per pending entry (30-day window, ledger cap 200), and each call does a complete get_media_pool_items() (library read + full proxy enrichment, or the whole API walk under one lock hold) to look for one old path. K pending moves = K walks of the same pool inside poll_once; a move in a rarely opened project re-costs every switch.
cost: 10 pending moves on a 1,300-clip project: 55-94 s with the watcher not polling and Resolve's scripting saturated; on a 20k-clip pool, tens of minutes per project switch.
fix: Walk the pool once per _relink_pending_moves call and match all pending entries against it (relink_moved taking pre-walked items); run it on a worker thread, not in the watcher callback. Keep 'only a walk that found the old path retires the entry'.

title: Every relink builds Resolve's full 60-key property dict two to four times plus a fresh connection, while the probed one-arg reader sits unused
what: replace_clip (_file_path_locked/_geometry_locked), link_proxy_media and clip_proxy_state call no-arg GetClipProperty() (12.5 ms) although _clip_property already probes the one-arg overload (0.1 ms) once per process and falls back; _before_mutation adds a forced fresh connect + 3 RPCs per clip.
cost: Per GOTCHAS 16 figures: 1,300-clip FIX ALL / auto proxy relink = 1,300 x (25-50 ms dict + ~65 ms connect) = ~2-2.5 min of extra _API_LOCK time, blocking watcher, b-roll insert and Cards; force refreshes double the geometry reads.
fix: Route those readers through _clip_property (two one-arg reads for geometry); let _before_mutation reuse the cached handle from comp-resolve-2 while keeping the max_age=0 project check. Keep File Path change as the success test.

title: The undo journal rewrites the whole JSON file for every entry (quadratic)
what: record() re-reads, re-parses and re-writes (indent=1, tmp + os.replace) the burst's entire journal per entry, so a burst is O(n^2) in CPU and bytes written.
cost: Measured 1,000 entries 3.7 s, 2,000 entries 13.9 s, final 779 KB, ~780 MB written for one 2,000-clip pass; at the 5,000 cap an estimated ~85 s and ~2 GB. Spent on the relink thread outside _API_LOCK.
evidence: probe journal_probe.py with HOME redirected to scratch.
fix: Keep the open burst in memory and write from it without re-reading, without indent, coalesced (every N entries or 1 s, at burst end, before an undo reads); or JSONL sidecar compacted at burst end. Keep valid JSON after a crash.

title: The CR-68 probe snapshots every process even when nothing listens on 1144, and the disconnection text spawns tasklist every 30 s on top
what: ABSENT is decided from TCP rows alone but every probe also walks a Toolhelp snapshot of all processes; every failed poll's describe_disconnection() spawns tasklist when its 30 s cache lapses, answering a question the snapshot already answered.
cost: Measured 9.2 ms CPU per probe, 8.4 ms of it the snapshot; >= 1 probe per 3 s = ~260 s CPU/day per machine; plus 2 tasklist spawns/min (~209 ms wall, ~19 ms CPU) = 2,880 spawns/day whenever Resolve is closed or unscriptable.
evidence: probe probe.py (tcp 0.27 ms, processes 8.41 ms); tasklist timing.
fix: Return ABSENT from the TCP rows before taking the snapshot (or OpenProcess only the listener/client pids); have _resolve_process_present reuse a Toolhelp snapshot instead of tasklist, keeping its fail-closed bias.

title: The Cards role's refusal watchdog runs PowerShell + WMI every 60 s for as long as a standalone agent is running
what: With cards_agent on and the role refused because a standalone reorder_web.py --agent is running, the watchdog launches powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Process every minute indefinitely to re-read every command line.
cost: Measured 441-504 ms wall per run, ~114 KB stdout, ~220 ms PowerShell CPU plus WmiPrvSE work; 1,440 launches/day beside Resolve.
ledger: related to RES-7 (2026-09-04, cadence by design)
fix: Toolhelp snapshot first; only when a python/pythonw/node process exists, query CIM for those pids (-Filter ProcessId=...) or read command lines via NtQueryInformationProcess; keep cannot-tell = refuse.

title: plan_relinks re-stats up to four proxy candidates for every clip without a working proxy on every 120 s pass, with no memory
what: find_proxy_on_disk tries 2 extensions x 2 spellings per clip each pass with os.path.exists; the watcher memoises the same question for 60 s and app._media_presence caches originals, but nothing caches the proxies' absence.
cost: Wired rig (local_root on SMB), 5,000-clip pool without Proxy/ files: up to 20,000 failed SMB stats per 120 s (estimated 20-40 s per pass); 80,000 at 20k clips, beyond the interval.
ledger: related to ops-efficiency-8 / CR-66 (FIXED for originals only)
fix: One listdir per distinct Proxy/ directory per pass with set lookups, or share the watcher's TTL memo; cache absence for at most one pass.

title: Every companion start walks the whole of local_root for *.ccsync-tmp, which on the base rig and wired rigs is the NAS share
what: Startup os.walks every directory under local_root to find interrupted FIX ALL partials and reservations; where local_root is the SMB share that is a full NAS tree enumeration per start, and starts are frequent (supervisor relaunch, OTA, stale-bridge self-restart after each Resolve quit).
cost: 50,000 files locally 0.12-0.35 s (measured); over SMB estimated 40-200 s of NAS metadata load per start at 100 projects, more at 500.
evidence: fixer.py:795; app.py:10581-10587; app.py:4966 (restart on Resolve exit).
fix: fix_clip records each tmp/reservation it creates in a small state file; sweep only those, falling back to the full walk when the file is absent or local_root is a local disk.
